target_customer: Municipalities, regions and private care providers in Nordic healthcare and social care, plus temp healthcare workers
problem: Care providers fill shifts by email, text and spreadsheets and struggle with scheduling and temp staffing during healthcare labor shortages.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus staffing marketplace take rate
product_category: Healthcare workforce scheduling and staffing marketplace

founders.name: Benjamin Waye
founders.background_notes: Named CEO and co-founder in TechCrunch, July 2022.

founders.name: Alexander Björkenstam
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and as press contact in the seed release.

founders.name: Edvin Fernqvist
founders.background_notes: YC page says he sourced PPE and saw staffing problems working with ICU staff.

competitors.name: Vivian Health
competitors.what: Healthcare job marketplace for travel nurses

competitors.name: Lantum
competitors.what: Locum and shift staffing platform for healthcare in the UK

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling optimization with preferences and labor rules, plus marketplace features; standard engineering with constraint-solving.

defensibility.rationale: Public sector contracts and a shared temp worker pool raise switching costs, while scheduling software is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals focused on other regions; Bemlo expanded into Norway and the UK and acquired Vivium.

market_need_then: Nurse shortages and heavy reliance on temp staffing in Nordic healthcare; founders saw it first-hand during COVID-19.

branding.domain_note: Uses bemlo.com. Legal entity is Bemalong AB.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B care sector tone, replaces emails and spreadsheets

branding.community_and_virality: Seed covered by TechCrunch, Tech.eu, EU-Startups and Arctic Startup

brand_strength.rationale: Press coverage across several outlets and a distinctive short name, but no evidence of community or mascot.

pivots.to: AI-driven scheduling and workforce management platform plus marketplace
pivots.why: Date approximate; company now emphasizes scheduling and acquired Vivium workforce software in February 2024, reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Bemlo raised a $3.3M seed in August 2022, grew to serve 39 municipalities, regions and private providers, and acquired Vivium in February 2024. It combined a staffing marketplace with scheduling software sold to public sector buyers. No Series A was found, so total funding remains modest and the company's scale rests on customer growth.
notes: Seed confirmed by company press release, TechCrunch and Tech.eu. ZoomInfo names Harlem Capital as lead while others do not, and Seedtable lists $3.8M across 3 rounds including a pre-seed; not recorded. Vivium acquisition source is a company announcement copy on test domains with a 2024-02-20 or 2024-03-22 date conflict; the Bemlo site news list says 22 Mar 2024. Competitor sources are TechCrunch July 2022, a few months after the W22 batch. The Hub says founded 2019; not otherwise verified. No outcome news beyond the acquisition.
